title: Rigveda 9.23: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.23: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.23 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 677r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.23.1-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 677r
translation.original_text:
1somā̍ asṛgram ā̱śavo̱ madho̱r mada̍sya̱ dhāra̍yā | a̱bhi viśvā̍ni̱ kāvyā̍ ||
2anu̍ pra̱tnāsa̍ ā̱yava̍ḥ pa̱daṁ navī̍yo akramuḥ | ru̱ce ja̍nanta̱ sūrya̍m ||
3ā pa̍vamāna no bharā̱ryo adā̍śuṣo̱ gaya̍m | kṛ̱dhi pra̱jāva̍tī̱r iṣa̍ḥ ||
4a̱bhi somā̍sa ā̱yava̱ḥ pava̍nte̱ madya̱m mada̍m | a̱bhi kośa̍m madhu̱ścuta̍m ||
5somo̍ arṣati dharṇa̱sir dadhā̍na indri̱yaṁ rasa̍m | su̱vīro̍ abhiśasti̱pāḥ ||
6indrā̍ya soma pavase de̱vebhya̍ḥ sadha̱mādya̍ḥ | indo̱ vāja̍ṁ siṣāsasi ||
7a̱sya pī̱tvā madā̍nā̱m indro̍ vṛ̱trāṇy a̍pra̱ti | ja̱ghāna̍ ja̱ghana̍c ca̱ nu ||
translation.text:
1SWIFT Soma drops have been effused in streams of meath, the gladdening drink, For sacred lore of every kind.
2Hither to newer. resting-place the ancient Living Ones are come. They made the Sun that he might shine.
3O Pavamâna, bring to us the unsacrificing foeman's wealth, And give us food with progeny.
4The living Somas being cleansed diffuse exhilarating drink, Turned to the vat which drips with meath.
5Soma flows on intelligent, possessing sap and mighty strength, Brave Hero who repels the curse.
6For Indra, Soma! thou art cleansed, a feast-companion for the Gods:
7When he had drunken draughts of this, Indra smote down resistless foes: Yea, smote them, and shall smite them still.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 677r (numbered 99r by the scribe) (OPenn image 677, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.22.7 ‹gavyāni dhārayaḥ tatam tantum›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 677v (numbered 99v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.24.3 ‹nṛ-bhiḥ yataḥ vi nīyase›. Verses 9.23.1-7 end on this page.
